nodes.description: External view function that pseudo-randomly selects a winner from a calldata address array using keccak256 over block values and an entropy salt.
Calldata address array of candidate participants supplied by the caller; its length drives the modulo operation and its elements are indexed by the derived winner index.
Caller-supplied uint256 salt mixed into the keccak256 entropy hash; fully controllable by the caller.
Local variable holding users.length; used both as hash input and as the modulo divisor for winner selection.
Local bytes32 keccak256 digest over address(this), block.number, block.timestamp, block.coinbase, block.gaslimit, block.difficulty, a past blockhash, size and salt.
Local uint256 index computed as uint256(hash) % size and used to index the users array.
Block timestamp consumed as entropy for the winner-selection hash, making the outcome miner/validator-influenced.
Weak on-chain randomness: keccak256 over block.timestamp and other block fields is predictable/manipulable by the block producer.
Modulo-bounded array indexing users[uint256(hash) % size]; reverts when size is zero and relies on the weak randomness for its result.

selectWinner executes the modulo/index computation on the users array.

block.timestamp flows into the entropy hash, making winnerIndex timestamp dependent.
The untrusted block timestamp is the entropy source of the unsafe randomness operation.
winnerIndex = uint256(hash) % size derives from the hash digest.
The keccak256 digest over block values is consumed as the pseudo-random value.
winnerIndex is the value used to index users in the selection step.
